contract: §56m The tag names a note's front matter gives through its `tags:` lists, read as `tag::extract_frontmatter_tags` reads them: an inline list `tags: [a, b]` split at its commas, or the `- item` lines after a `tags:` line, indented or not, up to the first line that is not one; each entry trimmed, then its double and then its single quotes taken off, then every leading `#` (`tag::bare_tag`); empty names left out; case as written. `frontmatter` is the text between the two `---` lines, as `md::split_frontmatter` gives it. The Rust test `tag::frontmatter::tests::the_reader_agrees_with_the_shared_fixture` reads this file; another reader of front-matter tags (the app reads them in TypeScript too) can read it to agree. These are a line reader's answers, not a YAML parser's: where `yaml` 2.9.1 or `js-yaml` 4.3.2 rejects the text or reads a different value for the list (2026-10-26), `why` says so; a YAML value keeps the `#`s this reader takes off, which no case repeats. `cases` are front matters to read; `names` (see `names_contract`) are names to rename to. Every character outside ASCII is written as a JSON unicode escape. A case may also carry `frontendTags` and `frontendWhy`: the names the app's frontend reader (`readFrontmatterLists` in `src/utils/markdown/frontmatter-list.ts`) gives where it reads the text differently on purpose — it does not split an inline list at a comma inside a quoted entry, so that its writer keeps the entry whole. The Rust test reads `tags`; the frontend's test (`src/utils/__tests__/frontmatter-tag-readers.test.ts`) reads `frontendTags` where a case has it.

names_contract: `names`: new tag names, with their leading `#`s already off, and what `tag::rename_tag` does with each. `accepted` follows the rule on `rename_tag`: the body's reader reads `#name` back as the whole name, the name is not `-` alone, and it has a base character (not every character is default-ignorable or a combining mark). For an accepted name, `bare` is how it is written into a bare list entry (no quote character, no leading `#`) by `frontmatter::yaml_string`: plain only when the plain-spelling rule allows it (a letter, digit or `_` first, then letters, marks, digits and `_-./`) and no YAML reader would read it as something other than text; quoted otherwise. These rows are the contract any copy of the rule is held to, in Rust or another language; the Rust test `tag::frontmatter::tests::the_new_name_rule_agrees_with_the_shared_fixture` reads them. Every row uses characters old enough to be in every Unicode table the two languages ship.
